nodes.description: A partial rather than complete failure of primary hemostatic plug consolidation, explaining why clinical bleeding is generally milder than in alphaIIbbeta3 or GPIb-IX-V deficiency: initial vWF-mediated adhesion, P2Y1 shape change, the primary reversible aggregation wave, and integrin alphaIIbbeta3 abundance are preserved, whereas ADP-driven autocrine amplification that stabilizes the platelet thrombus under shear is lost. nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic variants in P2RY12 abolish or severely impair platelet P2Y12 receptor activity through three documented molecular mechanisms. First, null alleles — including frameshift deletions causing premature truncation (such as c.378delC / p.Thr126fs*34) and large whole-allele genomic P2RY12 deletions transmitted in trans — eliminate functional surface receptor expression and reduce platelet [33P]2MeS-ADP binding sites. Second, signaling-defective missense variants in transmembrane helix 6 (p.Arg256Gln) and extracellular loop 3 (p.Arg265Trp) preserve normal surface expression and ligand-binding affinity while impairing post-occupancy receptor signal transduction. Third, substitution within the conserved GPCR DRY motif (p.Arg122Cys) triggers agonist-independent receptor internalization and lysosomal trafficking, depleting cell-surface P2Y12. Quantitative binding assays alone miss the second class entirely.

nodes.description: The rate-limiting biochemical lesion. Wild-type P2Y12 is negatively coupled to adenylyl cyclase through Gi, lowering intracellular cyclic AMP upon ADP engagement. In patient platelets and CHO cells expressing mutant P2Y12, ADP fails to suppress prostaglandin E1- or forskolin-stimulated cyclic AMP accumulation, whereas P2Y1-mediated intracellular Ca2+ mobilization remains intact. Because elevated cyclic AMP tonically restrains platelet activation, failure to lower it leaves the platelet partially braked during thrombus growth.

nodes.description: The cellular defect has two linked components. First, the sustained, irreversible phase of ADP-induced platelet aggregation is lost while P2Y1-dependent Ca2+ mobilization, shape change, and the initial small wave of aggregation remain intact, so platelet aggregation to ADP is incomplete and rapidly reversible even at high agonist concentrations (>=10 micromolar). Second, because secreted dense-granule ADP normally feeds back on P2Y12 to amplify secretion, ATP/dense-granule release and secondary aggregation in response to collagen, arachidonate, thromboxane analogue U46619, PAF, and epinephrine are markedly blunted despite normal granule stores.
